subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should OpenClaw add native PowerShell smoke coverage for these contributor commands in the existing Windows CI lane, and with which command set?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but adding recurring Windows CI work requires maintainer acceptance of command scope and runner cost, especially while the linked PR has proof and failure blockers.

options.title: Land focused pwsh smoke after proof
options.body: Keep this issue open until the linked PR or a replacement proves the selected commands pass under native PowerShell and the Windows runner cost is accepted.

options.title: Narrow the smoke commands
options.body: Start with only native PowerShell commands that already pass reliably, then track docs/build smoke expansion separately if needed.

options.title: Defer the CI lane
options.body: Leave the issue open or close by maintainer decision if the extra Windows runner time is not worth adding now.

recommendation.title: Land focused pwsh smoke after proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the linked PR or a replacement proves the selected commands pass under native PowerShell and the Windows runner cost is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties vincentkoc most strongly to CI runner budget, routing, and workflow guard decisions around this surface.
